figures.title: Architecture and evidence boundaries
figures.caption: ARCCRAFT procedural architecture and evidence boundaries. The specification layer registers the experiment, generates procedural worlds, separates stochastic streams, and validates states before simulation. The simulation layer links transitions and noncompensatory gates to replayable Failure Atlas records and reverse stress search, while the evaluation layer keeps computational replay distinct from empirical validation and classifies the resulting evidence as supported, mixed, or unsupported.

figures.title: Portfolio and temporal shift
figures.caption: Motor portfolio scale, outcome dynamics, and composition shift, 2022 to 2024. Panel A reports the growth from 67,172 to 168,133 policy year records. Panel B shows annual claim frequency and loss ratio, while Panel C shows the decline in the new business share from 97.91% to 57.34%, a 40.57 percentage point change that supports temporal rather than random evaluation. Source: public Spanish motor insurance portfolio, 2022 to 2024.

figures.title: Matched temporal forecasts
figures.caption: Temporal forecast performance across matched actuarial comparators. Panels A and B report aggregate errors relative to observed claim counts and incurred losses, where zero denotes perfect aggregate prediction. Panels C and D report policy level Poisson deviance, where smaller values indicate better predictive discrimination; policy level frequency improves deviance in both years, but the policy level cost model produces a pronounced 2023 aggregate error and never dominates the pooled cost comparator. Source: retrospective ARCCRAFT benchmark using the public Spanish motor insurance portfolio.

figures.title: Calibration and interval coverage
figures.caption: Risk decile calibration and process interval coverage. Panels A and B plot observed to predicted ratios by predicted risk decile, with 1.00 denoting perfect calibration; the lowest predicted risk groups are materially underpredicted, particularly for 2024 incurred loss. Panels C and D normalize predictions and their 95% process only intervals to the observed aggregate, showing count coverage in 2023, count misses in 2024, and incurred loss misses for every comparator and year. Source: retrospective ARCCRAFT benchmark using the public Spanish motor insurance portfolio.

figures.title: Frequency–severity stress surface
figures.caption: Frequency and severity stress surface for the motor portfolio. Panel A reports the mean simulated loss ratio for the 25 combinations of frequency and severity multipliers, with the outlined cell identifying the joint 25% stress. Panel B follows the equal multiplier path and shows the 95% process interval; the joint 1.25 multiplier produces a mean loss ratio of 1.11, above the technical threshold of 1.00. Source: registered ARCCRAFT stress simulations using the retrospective motor calibration.

figures.title: Scenario classes and failure gates
figures.title_fr: Classes de scénarios et seuils d’échec
figures.caption: Scenario class failure rates and Failure Atlas composition. Panel A reports failures among accepted worlds for each registered scenario class in the canonical 10,000 world run, from 0.00% under Baseline to 49.88% under Severe plausible conditions; Exploratory worlds remain analytically separate. Panel B reports atlas events on a logarithmic axis and shows that 3,588 traceability failures dominate one combined ratio failure and five structural rejections, so the experiment primarily tests the operational gate rather than actuarial insolvency detection. Source: canonical ARCCRAFT run, registered seed 20260825.

figures.title: Ablations and stream isolation
figures.caption: Procedural ablations, computational cost, and stream isolation. Panel A compares failures among accepted worlds with the broader failure or rejection measure across three registered runs per configuration; strict rejection creates the largest divergence because repaired worlds become structural rejections. Panel B reports mean runtime with one standard deviation, while Panel C shows exact replay in all 15 runs and confirms that named streams preserve claims and behavioural outputs after 100 irrelevant world draws, whereas a shared stream does not. Source: ARCCRAFT ablation and stream isolation experiments at registered seeds 20260825, 20260826, and 20260827.

abstract: Insurance stress tests commonly apply predefined shocks or simulate losses from static frequency–severity models. These approaches estimate adverse outcomes but do not necessarily integrate scenario sequencing, structural consistency, deterministic replay, and failure attribution. This paper proposes ARCCRAFT (Actuarial Risk & Contingency Computational, Reproducible Architecture for Failure Testing), a versioned procedural architecture in which synthetic insurance worlds evolve over multiple periods under explicit states, transitions, bounds, stochastic streams, and failure predicates. The evaluation separates computational verification from empirical prediction. First, a retrospective motor-insurance study uses 354,140 policy-year observations from 2022–2024 and two temporal forecast origins. Policy-level Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood frequency modelling reduces held-out count deviance from 0.8481 to 0.7871 in 2023 and from 0.9153 to 0.8330 in 2024, but does not improve every aggregate error. A policy-level cost model is unstable across years: its incurred-loss error is +9.58% in 2023 and −4.44% in 2024. No model covers observed incurred loss with its process-only interval, and no model covers the 2024 claim count. Second, a synthetic ablation study using three seeds and 10,000 worlds per configuration establishes exact local replay and shows that named PCG64 substreams isolate claim and behavioural results from irrelevant world-stream consumption. Validator and transition ablations alter the selected population and coded failure rates, but the full model’s failures are almost entirely generated by its operational traceability gate. The results support ARCCRAFT as a reproducible audit and diagnostic architecture in the inspected environment; they do not establish calibrated scenario plausibility, general predictive superiority, causal failure attribution, or external validity. Independent portfolios, claim-level losses, operational labels, and prospectively untouched forecast periods are required for confirmatory validation.
title: Procedural Stress Testing of Actuarial Models: Design and Preliminary Evaluation of the ARCCRAFT Framework

Categorical variable describing the main coverage structure of the motor insurance policy. The original detailed combinations have been grouped into broader, actuarially meaningful categories.
- TP: Basic third-party liability coverage only.
- TPG: Third-party liability with glass coverage.
- CC: Third-party liability combined with two or more additional coverages, such as theft, fire, total loss or glass.
- COMP_E: comprehensive with excess.
- COMP_N: comprehensive without excess
